results.title: Fix: Dangerous Code Execution Function Could Allow External Attacks in scrapy/shell.py
results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 960 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue
results.accepted_requirement: The system shall not evaluate content that could be defined by external sources as code.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall execute shell commands without evaluating content that could be defined by external sources as code.

issues: The requirement introduces 'execute shell commands' as a positive action, but the evidence only describes a vulnerability in eval() usage; nothing in the evidence states that shell command execution is the system behaviour being modified.
The requirement mixes two obligations: performing shell command execution and avoiding evaluation of externally-sourced content as code, but only the second is grounded in the evidence.
revision_instructions: Remove the clause about executing shell commands: the evidence does not state that shell command execution is a behaviour being changed or guaranteed, only that eval() was flagged as dangerous.

State the single grounded obligation directly, in the form that the system must not evaluate content that could be defined by external sources as code, without asserting an unrelated 'execute shell commands' action.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall not evaluate content that could be defined by external sources as code.

issues: This resolves the previous round's issue by removing the unsupported 'execute shell commands' clause and stating the single grounded obligation.

iteration_history.candidate: The system shall process exported data without executing arbitrary code embedded in the serialized data.

retrieved_requirements.statement: The system shall not evaluate content that could be defined by external sources as code.
The system shall prevent untrusted input from causing arbitrary code to be loaded and executed when generating a spider.
The system shall prevent untrusted input from causing arbitrary code modules to be loaded and executed during spider generation.

relations.reason: Both state a general prohibition on executing/evaluating externally-supplied data as code, though this one is scoped to exported/serialized data specifically.

issues: The requirement captures the security behaviour implied by the pickle vulnerability report (avoiding arbitrary code execution when serialized data is processed) without naming the mechanism (pickle) or asserting an unconfirmed remedy (JSON format), which matches the black-box-testable framing given in the definitions.
This overlaps with the requirement from Pull Request #6869, which states a similarly generic prohibition against evaluating externally-defined content as code.
